summary: Today’s pulse tracks Keeping cool without AC: Our readers share their tips, Spain’s Sánchez blames trafficking gangs as estimated 60,000 migrants reach Ceuta – Europe live, and Chancellor confirms Autumn budget will be delivered on 28 October – UK politics live. Across NPR, Guardian, and BBC, the strongest repeated signals are blanche, slush, and trump. In the background, Trump defends $1.8bn slush fund that is holding up Todd Blanche confirmation and Trump attacks Republican senator and defends $1.8bn slush fund amid Blanche nomination standoff – live keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: Keeping cool without AC: Our readers share their tips
headlines.description: We asked our readers to tell us how they've fended off heat without the refrigerant blasts of an air conditioner. Here's what they shared.

headlines.title: Spain’s Sánchez blames trafficking gangs as estimated 60,000 migrants reach Ceuta – Europe live
headlines.description: PM says criminals have misled people over a recent court ruling about those arriving in Spain via the sea Spanish prime minister Pedro Sánchez is now in Ceuta, accompanied by interior minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska. He first visited the Tarajal border crossing, and is now talking to officials from local authorities, border and police services.

headlines.title: Chancellor confirms Autumn budget will be delivered on 28 October – UK politics live
headlines.description: The chancellor says it will ‘give businesses and families some of the stability they need to plan for the future’ The construction of a new Chinese “super-embassy” in London, which is set to be built near the Tower of London, can go ahead after a high court challenge against the decision to grant planning permission was dismissed, PA Media is reporting. The Royal Mint Court Residents’ Association (RMCRA) brought legal action against the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government and the London Borough of Tower Hamlets.

headlines.title: Trump defends $1.8bn slush fund that is holding up Todd Blanche confirmation
headlines.description: President calls for former personal defense lawyer to be ‘immediately approved’ as attorney general Donald Trump has defended controversial plans for a $1.8bn slush fund even as they threaten to derail the nomination of his former personal lawyer Todd Blanche for US attorney general. Blanche “should be immediately approved” by the US Senate, the president declared in a post on his Truth Social platform on Friday morning, defending the payout scheme proposed by his officials in the Department of Justice as it holds up Blanche’s confirmation.

headlines.title: Trump attacks Republican senator and defends $1.8bn slush fund amid Blanche nomination standoff – live
headlines.description: Trump says John Cornyn, who is questioning Todd Blanche’s attorney general nomination, didn’t have a problem with IRS slush fund until he didn’t endorse the senator in Texas primary Stevens quoted-tweeted a video of El-Sayed talking about massive outside funding from the groups affiliated with American Israel Public Affairs Committee (Aipac), where El-Sayed said Aipac should “come for me” and called Stevens “the least capable candidate in America”.

headlinePool.title: UK petrol price hits Iran war high, adding to pressure on households
headlinePool.description: Average pump price reaches 160p a litre, while diesel is up 14.5p to 179p and forecast to increase to 185p soon Business live – latest updates The price of petrol has hit a new Iran war high at UK forecourts, adding to the financial pressure on millions of households about to embark on their annual holiday. The RAC said that in “very unwelcome news for drivers” the average pump price had reached 160p a litre, reversing the fall to 151p in early July that followed the announcement of a Middle East ceasefire .

headlinePool.title: About 60,000 migrants arrive in Ceuta in 24 hours, Spanish territory's leader says
headlinePool.description: Spain's prime minister described the situation as an "attack" on its North African territory and said all illegal migrants would be returned to Morocco.

headlinePool.title: Middle East crisis live: Hamas will hand over weapons to new Gaza administration, says official, but deal depends on Israeli withdrawal
headlinePool.description: Hamas’s Ghazi Hamad tells Reuters that it will hand over arms to body established by Trump’s Board of Peace Trump claims agreement for ‘complete disarmament’ of Hamas in Gaza but support uncertain Saudi Arabia prepares sea and possible land offensive against Houthis Al Jazeera reporter Hani Mahmoud has reported the mood in Gaza this morning following news of Hamas’s potential disarmament. Palestinians have heard repeated statements about their fate in the three years since the current war began between Israel and Hamas, so last night’s announcement by Donald Trump wasn’t met with any particular joy or celebration. “There is scepticism and cautiousness among Palestinians,” Mahoud writes from Gaza City in the north of the Strip.

headlinePool.title: Iran strikes tankers under US escort in Hormuz strait as Trump gathers cabinet to discuss war
headlinePool.description: Energy prices have soared again since fighting between US and Iran resumed two weeks ago as conflict spreads across Middle East Middle East crisis live – latest updates Iran has said it struck two tankers trying to pass through the strait of Hormuz under the escort of the US military as Donald Trump gathered his cabinet to discuss the stalling war and rising prices as midterm elections in the US loom. Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said on Friday that the “non-compliant oil tankers … were struck and brought to a halt, while four other oil tankers quickly changed course and returned to their previous positions”. The military body said the ships had tried to pass through the strait via an “undeclared route” and under US aerial escort.

headlinePool.title: FTSE 100 on track for best month since first US attacks on Iran five months ago – as it happened
headlinePool.description: Live, rolling coverage as London’s biggest companies defy Middle East disruption and UK petrol prices rise to around £1.60 per litre, the highest since Donald Trump ordered renewed strikes The story piquing the interest of the financial press this morning is that of Leopold Aschenbrenner , the AI Wunderkind (he’s German-born) who has been forced to sell off his fund in a fire sale after the AI boom ran out of steam. The 24-year-old had persuaded a lot of people to give him a lot of money for a hedge fund, after previously working for OpenAI and the FTX Future Fund, a charitable arm of the fraudulent crypto empire of Sam Bankman-Fried, who is now in prison . Aschenbrenner ploughed that money into debt-fuelled bets on artificial intelligence companies, earning huge returns until he found out that stocks can also fall. The trader dubbed the “Nostradamus of AI” would have been hard-pressed to foresee how quickly his high-flying hedge fund would run into trouble. The firm’s rapid downward spiral is a familiar tale, as Silicon Valley and Wall Street once again threw their weight behind a bright-eyed but untested investor who promised this time would be different. “Everybody always wants to find the next golden child,” said one longtime hedge fund executive. “It just keeps happening.” In less than 24 hours — which included a conversation between Griffin and Aschenbrenner — Griffin’s Citadel hedge fund reached out to Situational Awareness and snapped up the investments at a discount, according to a person familiar with the matter who asked not to be identified citing private information. It was a startling reversal for Aschenbrenner, a former researcher at OpenAI who – before starting his hedge fund roughly two years ago — had no previous investment experience. His fledging firm has watched its assets plunge from $45bn at the start of July to about $10bn.

headlinePool.title: Trump says ‘complete disarmament’ of Hamas agreed in Gaza but Israel yet to accept
headlinePool.description: US president hails breakthrough but Israeli far-right minister says ‘only solution’ is ‘encouraging emigration and destroying Hamas’ Middle East crisis – live updates What is Trump’s Board of Peace and who is involved? Donald Trump has declared a breakthrough in negotiations over the disarmament of Hamas in Gaza and the withdrawal of Israeli forces, issues that have so far stalled the implementation of last October’s ceasefire, but Israel has yet to respond officially to the plan and government officials have voiced scepticism over the deal. Announcing the agreement in a social media post on Thursday night, Trump said it involved the “complete disarmament” of Hamas and other armed groups in Gaza and was “a monumental step toward ending the fighting”.

headlinePool.title: Second police official in St Paul alleges sexual harassment by mayor
headlinePool.description: Kaohly Her is accused of inappropriate conduct and creating a ‘sexualized work environment’ by senior officials US politics live – latest updates A second senior police official in St Paul has alleged sexual harassment and inappropriate conduct by the Minnesota city’s Democratic mayor, Kaohly Her, following confirmation that an inquiry into her behavior was launched earlier this year. The new claims were reported on Thursday by the Minnesota Star Tribune, which said it obtained further details of the mayor’s alleged actions that gave rise to the original complaint by Axel Henry, the police chief of St Paul.

headlinePool.title: At least 43 people die as tens of thousands cross to Spanish enclave of Ceuta from Morocco
headlinePool.description: Pedro Sánchez decries ‘violation of territorial integrity’ as other EU countries criticise Madrid over incident Europe live – latest updates At least 43 people have died trying to reach the Spanish enclave of Ceuta after as many as 50,000 migrants entered the tiny territory from Morocco in a matter of hours, triggering a political crisis for the Madrid government and unleashing a barrage of criticism from other EU countries. The large influx of people arriving in Ceuta by swimming across from neighbouring Morocco or scaling the border fence has caught the city of 85,000 off guard and resulted in what one local police association called a “serious humanitarian crisis”.

headlinePool.description: The AI chatbot was more effective at creating “exploitable trust” than the humans.
